edges.description: LIN28B blockade of let-7 maturation is the route by which this node lowers mature let-7. The measurement behind the edge is in neuroblastoma cells rather than in patient tumours.

Mature let-7 represses MYCN post-transcriptionally, so depleting let-7 de-represses MYCN protein and feeds the proliferative programme the receiving node describes. This route is post-transcriptional, so it reaches that node without MYCN amplification. The measurement behind the edge is in neuroblastoma cells rather than in patient tumours.

Loss of the let-7 restraint blocks differentiation of normal neuroblasts and of neuroblastoma cells, reaching from the microRNA axis the same arrest the receiving node describes. The differentiation block is reported for the whole LIN28B-let-7-MYCN axis rather than for the let-7 step alone, and releasing mature let-7 in neuroblastoma cells inhibits MYCN activity and shifts the cells toward differentiation, which is the same link read in the restoring direction.
intermediate_mechanisms: De-repression of MYCN protein following loss of post-transcriptional let-7 repression

edges.description: MYCN amplification drives aggressive proliferation

The arrested neural crest-derived sympathoadrenal progenitor is the lineage within which the two tumour cell identities are defined. The noradrenergic pole carries the committed sympathetic core regulatory circuitry, while the mesenchymal (NCC-like) pole sits close to the undifferentiated neural crest cell, so the two states map onto different points of the same blocked differentiation programme. The evidence cited here locates the two identities in that lineage; it does not show that the arrest itself drives switching between them.

Arrest at an immature noradrenergic sympathoadrenal stage leaves the lineage's norepinephrine-uptake machinery in place. The edge is retention, not induction: the transporter is inherited from the sympathetic neuronal precursor rather than switched on by the arrest, and the cited sources state lineage-linked expression rather than any inducing step. It is recorded as an edge because the arrested lineage state is what accounts for the transporter still being there, which is the fact the therapy depends on.

Amplified MYCN tracks a T-cell-poor microenvironment. In primary tumours from patients with metastatic disease a T-cell-poor microenvironment was associated with genomic MYCN amplification, and in a separate patient series high-risk MYCN-not-amplified tumours carried significantly higher cytotoxic tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte signatures than MYCN-amplified tumours. The route recorded here runs through suppressed interferon and pro-inflammatory signalling and the chemokine output that recruits T cells: in human and murine neuroblastoma cell lines N-Myc suppresses interferon and pro-inflammatory pathways, and N-Myc depletion amplified the interferon response to a cGAS-STING agonist, which in turn raised chemokine expression including Cxcl10 and drew T cells in a microfluidics migration assay. The limits sit on both halves. The patient half is an association in cross-sectional cohorts and does not establish direction, and the second series contrasts MYCN-not-amplified against MYCN-amplified tumours, so the direction is read off that contrast rather than measured within tumours over time. The intermediates are cell-line and microfluidics results; the cGAS-STING agonist used is specific for mouse and not human STING, so that arm was run in murine lines, and nothing in the model half was measured in patient tumours.
intermediate_mechanisms: N-Myc suppression of interferon and pro-inflammatory pathway activity
Reduced chemokine expression, including CXCL10, and reduced cytotoxic T-cell recruitment

edges.description: Amplified MYCN raises TERT transcription, which makes MYCN amplification a route to telomerase activation rather than a separate telomere maintenance mechanism. TERT expression was higher in MYCN-amplified tumours, and in a MYCN-amplified cell line TERT was the gene most strongly downregulated when MYCN was knocked down. Not every MYCN-amplified tumour takes this route: some express TERT as low as ALT tumours do, and forced MYCN overexpression did not induce TERT where the promoter was repressed.
intermediate_mechanisms: Increased TERT transcription driven by amplified MYCN

edges.description: MYCN regulates SLC3A2, the transporter that carries polyamine uptake in neuroblastoma, alongside other components of the polyamine pathway, so amplified MYCN raises the import route as well as the synthesis route. As with the synthesis edge below, no return edge is drawn from the uptake node into this one, to avoid a two-node cycle in the pathograph.
edges.target: Compensatory Polyamine Uptake from the Microenvironment

edges.description: ODC1, the rate-limiting enzyme of polyamine synthesis, is a direct transcriptional target of MYCN, so amplified MYCN raises flux through the pathway. The dependence runs the other way as well, which is what makes the pathway a target rather than only a consequence, but that return relation is recorded in the downstream node's description rather than as a second edge, because an edge back into this node would make a two-node cycle in the pathograph.

In MYCN-amplified tumours the MYCN transcript is itself abundant enough to act as a competing endogenous RNA for let-7, which is why deleting LIN28B from amplified cell lines leaves MYCN protein and growth intact. This is the least established of the three routes into let-7 depletion: the authors raise the stoichiometric question themselves, whether a rise of more than 100-fold in MYCN mRNA, which lifts the total pool of let-7 target sites by only about a quarter, suffices for a competing-endogenous-RNA effect, and answer it with their own 3-prime-UTR-loss reporter and let-7-target mRNA sequencing. The quantification is in MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cell lines.

Amplified MYCN also raises LIN28B itself, closing a loop with the let-7 node: MYCN binds the LIN28B promoter directly in a neuroblastoma line carrying inducible MYCN, and acts in parallel through miR-26a-5p. This edge records the transcriptional arm only and makes no claim about which arm dominates in a given tumour.

N-Myc is what puts the replication checkpoint under load, so the dependence on CHK1 and WEE1 follows the oncogene rather than sitting beside it. Two results in one study carry the link: CHK1 inhibitor sensitivity tracked total MYC(N) protein, and inducing MYCN in untransformed retinal pigment epithelial cells was by itself enough to phosphorylate CHK1. The second is the causal half, and it is deliberately run outside neuroblastoma, because isolating what MYCN alone does requires a cell that does not already carry the amplification. That is also what keeps it a model rather than a measurement in the disease, which is why the edge is graded indirect. What this edge leaves out is the replication stress itself, the step between the oncogene and the checkpoint it activates.
intermediate_mechanisms: Replication stress generated by MYCN-driven proliferation, which is not measured in this experiment
Phosphorylation of CHK1, reported at Ser345 and Ser296 in high-risk primary tumours on the target node

edges.description: By holding N-Myc protein above what growth-factor signalling would sustain, the interaction keeps the MYCN-driven transcriptional programme running. The dependency runs the other way as well, since amplified tumours are the ones that need AURKA, but no return edge is drawn, to avoid a two-node cycle in the pathograph.

The two amplicon classes are what account for the regulatory requirements of MYCN overexpression, so the amplicon's architecture sits upstream of MYCN protein dosage and thereby of MYCN-driven proliferation. The architecture sets the regulatory route rather than gating the outcome: class II amplicons lacking the key local enhancers nevertheless expressed relatively high MYCN per gene copy, which is what the authors mean by ectopic enhancer hijacking compensating for the loss of local elements. Neither cited sentence reaches proliferation, so MYCN overexpression is named as the intermediate.
intermediate_mechanisms: Sustained MYCN overexpression from the co-amplified or hijacked CRC-driven enhancer

edges.description: Because ecDNA segregates asymmetrically at mitosis, carrying the amplicon extrachromosomally rather than in a chromosomal array is what produces variation in oncogene dosage between cells of the same tumour. The cited sentence is the general statement of that property of ecDNA rather than a measurement in neuroblastoma; the measurements sit on the downstream node.

Activating ALK kinase-domain mutations found in neuroblastoma signal into the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade, which is why relapse series count ALK among the RAS-MAPK-activating lesions while this entry models the receptor on this node rather than listing ALK among the pathway node's genes. The edge says that RAS-MAPK signalling is one output of the activated receptor, not its only one.
intermediate_mechanisms: Receptor-proximal adaptor recruitment and GTP loading of RAS downstream of the activated kinase, omitted from this edge.

edges.description: Constitutive ALK kinase signalling converges on the same proliferative output as MYCN amplification and co-operates with it; ALK-mutant and MYCN-amplified disease frequently co-occur and jointly enhance malignancy.

Surface GD2 is the antigen the therapeutic antibodies bind, so it is the precondition for antibody-mediated killing. This edge is intervention-conditioned: it carries flux only while an anti-GD2 antibody is being given, and the downstream node describes what the drug then does rather than anything the untreated tumor does.

Telomerase keeps telomeres from eroding, so tumour cells can go on dividing. High-risk neuroblastoma cell lines with neither telomerase activity nor ALT showed continuous telomere shortening, and most lost viability in culture.

RAS-MAPK-activating mutations are selected over the interval between diagnosis and relapse, in which most patients receive chemotherapy, and a paired series reads clonal selection for NF1 mutations as a candidate driver of therapy resistance. Neither series tests whether the pathway state confers resistance: neither relates RAS-MAPK status to treatment response or survival, so the intervening mechanism is undemonstrated and the edge is an association between a selected lesion class and relapse rather than a mechanism of resistance.

Among patients who relapsed, an inactivating TP53 mutation was independently prognostic for overall survival, and abolishing p53 function in p53-intact neuroblastoma cell lines is enough on its own to confer high-level resistance to several cytotoxic drugs. The patient evidence is a prognostic association rather than a demonstrated mechanism, and it is specific to the downstream limb of this node: in the same series the upstream MDM2 amplification and p14ARF inactivation were not associated with survival.

Loss of ATRX/DAXX complex function permits alternative lengthening of telomeres. ATRX mutation is associated with loss of nuclear ATRX protein and with ALT, and in one series every ALT tumour carried an ATRX or DAXX alteration. Without ATRX, histone H3.3 is not efficiently deposited at telomeric repeats, replication forks stall there, and the telomeres undergo the homologous recombination that leads to ALT.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of ATRX/DAXX-dependent deposition of histone H3.3 at telomeric repeats

edges.description: This entry reads the tumor's lymphoid response as feeding the autoimmunity. In a model drawn from tumor studies, polyclonal autoreactive B cells act as antigen-presenting cells and drive tertiary lymphoid structure formation, thereby supporting the paraneoplastic neuropathology; the authors present tumor and nervous-system involvement as parts of one systemic autoimmune process, the step from the tumor to the brain was not tested, and whether the tumor infiltrate arises from lymphocytes entering from the circulation is unsettled. A pathology review read the tumors' lymphoid infiltrate as suggesting an immune-mediated mechanism for the syndrome, and in one child the same B-cell clone was dominant in both the cerebrospinal fluid and the tumor. The intermediate steps are unknown.
edges.source: Intratumoral Lymphoid Infiltration with Lymphoid Follicles
edges.target: Cerebellar and Brainstem-Directed B- and T-Cell Autoimmunity

edges.description: In children with neuroblastoma, OMAS is described as a paraneoplastic disease characterized by autoimmunity directed at the cerebellum and brainstem, and that autoimmunity is taken to produce the syndrome's eye-movement, motor and behavioral signs; there is good evidence that OMAS is immune-mediated. The cited sources do not identify which immune effector acts on which neurons.
edges.source: Cerebellar and Brainstem-Directed B- and T-Cell Autoimmunity

edges.description: ALT maintains telomere length without telomerase, giving the tumour cells that use it an unlimited replicative capacity. High-risk neuroblastoma cell lines with neither ALT nor telomerase activity showed continuous telomere shortening, and most lost viability in culture.

The neurotrophin-deprivation account of spontaneous regression: a tumour whose cells have become dependent on NGF through TrkA regresses when NGF is not available in its microenvironment. The edge is indirect because no study has observed NGF becoming limiting in a regressing patient tumour; what the cited work measured is stated in the intermediate mechanisms below.
intermediate_mechanisms: Programmed death of TRKA-expressing tumour cells deprived of NGF, shown in cells cultured from TRK-expressing primary tumours rather than in a regressing tumour
Induction of the dependence receptor UNC5D with E2F1 and p53 on NGF withdrawal, shown in cultured cells from two primary favourable-biology tumours rather than in a regressing tumour

edges.description: The telomere-shortening account of spontaneous regression: a tumour that maintains its telomeres by neither route cannot sustain indefinite proliferation, so its telomere reserve is drawn down. The absence is proposed as a precondition for the tumour to involute or differentiate rather than as a sufficient cause: this entry's own Unlimited Replicative Potential node records high-risk tumours without significant telomere lengthening activity whose cells kept proliferating. The edge is indirect because the steps between the missing mechanism and the regression have not been observed in a regressing tumour, and because the source states the absence as a prerequisite, a necessary condition, rather than as a cause.
intermediate_mechanisms: Progressive telomere attrition ending in senescence, crisis or cell death, inferred from the absence of a maintenance mechanism rather than observed in a regressing tumour
edges.source: Absence of a Telomere Maintenance Mechanism

edges.description: An abdominal or pelvic primary, most often in or near the adrenal gland, can present as a palpable abdominal mass.
edges.source: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect

edges.description: An abdominal primary can distend the abdomen. The cited series lists distension among the signs of a tumor arising in the abdomen, separately from a palpable mass.
edges.source: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect

edges.description: An abdominal primary can cause abdominal pain. The cited series lists pain among the signs of a tumor arising in the abdomen but does not say how the tumor causes it.
edges.source: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect

edges.description: Horner syndrome arises mostly with localized disease, often with cervical or thoracic tumors, and can be the presenting sign. It is attributed to mass effect of the tumor on the sympathetic innervation of the eye; the cited series show its association with tumor site and localized disease rather than the nerve involvement itself. Horner syndrome can also follow surgical resection of the tumor, a complication of treatment that this edge does not cover.
intermediate_mechanisms: Tumor involvement of the cervical or upper thoracic sympathetic pathway to the eye
edges.source: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect

edges.description: A paravertebral tumor can extend through the neural foramina into the spinal canal and compress the spinal cord and/or nerve roots, causing radicular pain, motor deficit up to paraplegia, and sphincter dysfunction. Extension into the spinal canal does not always cause symptoms: in a prospective cohort selected for it, a third of the children were asymptomatic at enrollment.
edges.source: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect

edges.description: Compression of the renal artery or renal parenchyma by the tumor, with a renin-mediated rise in blood pressure, is the usual explanation offered for hypertension at diagnosis, and such hypertension frequently resolves after resection. The cited sources state this explanation rather than demonstrate it, and the link is contested. A registry survey of hypertensive children could not demonstrate a correlation between hypertension and compression of the renal vascular pedicle, although it found involvement of the renal pedicle to be the only risk factor consistently associated with hypertension persisting after surgery. In a single-center series of children with at least stage II hypertension, four had radiologic evidence of renal compression, but renin was normal in all four children in whom it was measured.
intermediate_mechanisms: Renin-mediated rise in blood pressure after compression of the renal artery or renal parenchyma
edges.source: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect

edges.description: Tumor cells spread from the primary tumor through the lymphatic and hematogenous systems and establish metastases at distant sites. Tumors with unfavorable clinical behavior combine locally invasive growth with widespread metastatic dissemination, and orbital metastases mostly arise from an abdominal primary.
intermediate_mechanisms: Locally invasive growth and spread of tumor cells through the lymphatic and hematogenous systems
edges.source: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect

edges.description: Skeletal and bone marrow metastases cause bone pain, which can be diffuse and intense enough to stop a child moving freely.
Orbital metastases infiltrating the periorbital bones cause proptosis and periorbital ecchymosis, often on both sides.

Infiltration of the bone marrow by tumor cells has been associated with anemia at diagnosis, in one series with infiltration by more than 10% malignant cells. The link is contested: two other series found anemia common in children with and without marrow infiltration and attributed it to iron or nutritional deficiency. The cited series report associations and do not measure how infiltration would lower red cell production.

Infiltration of the bone marrow by tumor cells has been associated with thrombocytopenia at diagnosis in two series, in one of them with infiltration by more than 10% malignant cells, although a third series found it no more frequent with marrow involvement than without. The cited series report associations and do not measure how infiltration lowers the platelet count.

In the INRGSS stage MS pattern the liver is the main metastatic site, and extensive liver involvement enlarges the liver, which in young infants can compress vital structures, with signs of pulmonary, renal or hepatic compromise.
Skin metastases can present as noncompressible, blue-purple subcutaneous nodules, part of the INRGSS stage MS pattern in young children.
VIP released by the tumor binds VPAC1 receptors on intestinal epithelial cells and causes secretory, watery diarrhea with ion disturbance; resection of the tumor relieves it.
intermediate_mechanisms: VIP binding to VPAC1 receptors on intestinal epithelial cells, driving intestinal fluid and electrolyte secretion

edges.description: The state switch is what produces the resistant fraction: cells at or moving towards the mesenchymal pole survive induction chemotherapy, so the mesenchymal proportion rises after treatment. The patient data behind this edge are observational and do not separate therapy-induced switching into the mesenchymal state from survival of mesenchymal cells already present.

Occupying the mesenchymal pole leaves the cells without ALK expression, and so without the drug target, which is why the escape follows from the cell state rather than from any change in ALK itself. Demonstrated in cell lines and in xenografts of those cells.
edges.target: ALK-Inhibitor Escape by Loss of Target Expression

edges.description: The state that confers chemotherapy resistance and ALK-inhibitor escape carries the opposite immune phenotype: the immune-enriched subset of neuroblastomas is the one characterised by mesenchymal lineage signatures, and mesenchymal-state cells are the ones cytotoxic lymphocytes recruit to and kill.

Supplies a molecular switch for the arrest this node asserts: multi-site phosphorylation of Ascl1 converts it from a driver of sympathoadrenal differentiation into an inert factor, matching the phospho-state Ascl1 is held in within neuroblastoma cells.
edges.limitations: Frog AVNA cells are a developmental counterpart of the presumed cell of origin, not tumour cells, and the model contains no transformed tissue — arrest is scored as failure to differentiate on schedule rather than as tumour formation. The link to human disease rests on the observed phospho-state of ASCL1 in neuroblastoma lines, so the model shows the state is sufficient to block differentiation, not that it is what maintains any patient's tumour.
edges.source: Xenopus anteroventral noradrenergic (AVNA) cell differentiation model

edges.description: Positions MYCN upstream of the differentiation block: MYCN overexpression prevents Ascl1-driven differentiation, and loses that ability when Ascl1 cannot be phosphorylated.
edges.limitations: This is the differentiation-blocking arm of MYCN only. The node is about proliferation, and no proliferative or tumour-growth readout was taken here; MYCN is introduced by overexpression in a normal embryo, not by the genomic amplification that defines high-risk neuroblastoma.
edges.source: Xenopus anteroventral noradrenergic (AVNA) cell differentiation model

edges.description: The model runs the LIN28B-to-let-7 arm forwards: driving LIN28B in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage produces tumours whose let-7 is low and whose MYCN protein is high.
edges.limitations: In a Lin28B mouse reported separately, sympathetic ganglion and adrenal medulla volume and Let-7a were unchanged despite a 12- to 17-fold rise in Lin28B, while Let-7a was strongly reduced in that line's tumour tissue. The let-7 arm of this model is therefore established in the tumours and not in normal developing sympathoadrenal tissue; do not read the mouse as evidence that let-7 depletion initiates the disease.

edges.target: c-MYC Activation by Enhancer Hijacking or Enhancer Amplification

nodes.description: A radiopharmaceutical given for MIBG-avid relapsed or refractory disease, in which the norepinephrine analogue carries iodine-131 into the tumor cell through the norepinephrine transporter. Eligibility turns on avidity: the randomized NANT phase II required at least one MIBG-avid site, and absence of avidity on a properly performed diagnostic scan is in principle a contraindication. Response figures from different designs are not comparable and are given separately. In that randomized trial the response rate after one course was 14% for MIBG alone, 14% with vincristine and irinotecan, and 32% with vorinostat; the trial used a pick-the-winner design, so the vorinostat arm is the one its design selected rather than one shown superior. Outside randomized comparison, a 164-patient phase II reported a 36% complete plus partial response rate, and a systematic review that identified no randomized controlled trials found objective response across 25 studies ranging from 0% to 75%, mean 32%. The frontline role is unproven: a Cochrane review found no randomized or controlled clinical trial comparing newly diagnosed high-risk regimens with and without the therapy, and could not make recommendations for its frontline use. One cohort of 106 relapsed or refractory patients found that markers of lower NET and VMAT2 protein expression were associated with a higher likelihood of response, while the NET H-score itself was not significantly associated with it.

evidence.reference_title: Randomized Phase II Trial of MIBG Versus MIBG, Vincristine, and Irinotecan Versus MIBG and Vorinostat for Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Report From NANT Consortium.
evidence.snippet: After one course, the response rates (partial response or better) on arms A, B, and C were 14% (95% CI, 5 to 30), 14% (5 to 31), and 32% (18 to 51).

evidence.reference_title: Randomized Phase II Trial of MIBG Versus MIBG, Vincristine, and Irinotecan Versus MIBG and Vorinostat for Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Report From NANT Consortium.
evidence.snippet: The trial was designed with 105 patients to ensure an 80% chance that the arm with highest response rate was selected.

evidence.reference_title: Phase II study on the effect of disease sites, age, and prior therapy on response to iodine-131-metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy in refractory neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: One hundred sixty-four patients with progressive, refractory or relapsed high-risk neuroblastoma, age 2 to 30 years, were treated in a limited institution phase II study.

evidence.reference_title: Phase II study on the effect of disease sites, age, and prior therapy on response to iodine-131-metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy in refractory neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: The overall complete plus partial response rate was 36%.

evidence.reference_title: A systematic review of 131I-meta iodobenzylguanidine molecular radiotherapy for neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: The objective tumour response rate reported in 25 studies ranged from 0% to 75%, mean 32%. We conclude that (131)I-mIBG is an active treatment for neuroblastoma, but its place in the management of neuroblastoma remains unclear.

evidence.reference_title: A systematic review of 131I-meta iodobenzylguanidine molecular radiotherapy for neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: No randomised controlled trials (RCTs) were identified.

evidence.reference_title: Iodine-131-meta-iodobenzylguanidine therapy for patients with newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: We identified no RCTs or CCTs comparing the effectiveness of treatment including 131I-MIBG therapy versus treatment not including 131I-MIBG therapy in patients with newly diagnosed HR NBL.

evidence.reference_title: Iodine-131-meta-iodobenzylguanidine therapy for patients with newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Based on the currently available evidence, we cannot make recommendations for the use of 131I-MIBG therapy in patients with newly diagnosed HR NBL in clinical practice.

evidence.reference_title: Norepinephrine transporter and vesicular monoamine transporter 2 tumor expression as a predictor of response to (131) I-MIBG in patients with relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Markers of lower NET and VMAT2 protein expression are associated with higher likelihood of response to 131 I-MIBG therapy in patients with relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma.

evidence.reference_title: Norepinephrine transporter and vesicular monoamine transporter 2 tumor expression as a predictor of response to (131) I-MIBG in patients with relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: NET H-score was not significantly associated with response (≥PR), though the percentage of tumor cells expressing NET was lower among responders (median 80% for ≥PR vs. 90% for <PR; p = .0014).

evidence.reference_title: Nervous system: Embryonal tumors: Neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: The primary predisposition genes in familial neuroblastoma are ALK and PHOX2B.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of ALK as a major familial neuroblastoma predisposition gene.
evidence.snippet: Our results demonstrate that heritable mutations of ALK are the main cause of familial neuroblastoma, and that germline or acquired activation of this cell-surface kinase is a tractable therapeutic target for this lethal paediatric malignancy.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of ALK as a major familial neuroblastoma predisposition gene.
evidence.snippet: Resequencing in 194 high-risk neuroblastoma samples showed somatically acquired mutations in the tyrosine kinase domain in 12.4% of samples.

evidence.reference_title: ALK mutations confer differential oncogenic activation and sensitivity to ALK inhibition therapy in neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: We describe comprehensive genomic, biochemical, and computational analyses of ALK mutations across 1,596 diagnostic neuroblastoma samples. ALK tyrosine kinase domain mutations occurred in 8% of samples--at three hot spots and 13 minor sites--and correlated significantly with poorer survival in high- and intermediate-risk neuroblastoma.

evidence.reference_title: Deep Sequencing Reveals Occurrence of Subclonal ALK Mutations in Neuroblastoma at Diagnosis.
evidence.snippet: In this series, deep sequencing allows the detection of F1174 and R1275 ALK mutational events at diagnosis in 10% of cases, with subclonal events in more than half of these, which would have gone undetected by Sanger sequencing.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic susceptibility to neuroblastoma: current knowledge and future directions.
evidence.snippet: It is estimated that gain-of-function mutations in ALK account for 75% of familial neuroblastoma.

evidence.reference_title: The Neuroblastoma Microenvironment, Heterogeneity and Immunotherapeutic Approaches.
evidence.snippet: Germline mutations in the anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene are found in 80% of familial cases

evidence.reference_title: Genome-wide linkage analysis to identify genetic modifiers of ALK mutation penetrance in familial neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Following a genome-wide linkage analysis and sequencing of candidate genes in the critical region, we identified ALK as the major familial NB gene. Dominant mutations in ALK are found in more than 50% of familial NB cases.

evidence.reference_title: Retinoblastoma and Neuroblastoma Predisposition and Surveillance.
evidence.snippet: Germline mutations in ALK and PHOX2B account for most familial NB cases.

evidence.reference_title: Neuroblastoma models for insights into tumorigenesis and new therapies.
evidence.snippet: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) mutation is also found in 7% of sporadic neuroblastomas and 50% of familial neuroblastomas.

evidence.reference_title: ALK mutations confer differential oncogenic activation and sensitivity to ALK inhibition therapy in neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Three 'hotspot' residues accounted for 85% of mutations (Figure 1, Table 1): R1275 (43%), F1174 (30%), and F1245 (12%)

evidence.reference_title: Retinoblastoma and Neuroblastoma Predisposition and Surveillance.
evidence.snippet: Germline mutations in ALK encode for single-base substitutions in key regions of the kinase domain that result in constitutive activation of the kinase, with the R1275Q mutation most frequently observed (Table 2).

nodes.description: ALK (anaplastic lymphoma kinase) is activated by point mutations in approximately 8-10% of neuroblastomas at diagnosis, and by amplification in additional cases. In neuroblastoma cells, high expression of the wild-type receptor can also lead to its constitutive activation. Intragenic rearrangement of the ALK locus is a third and rare route, found in four of 332 primary tumours screened, where the receptor is phosphorylated although no fusion protein is predicted. ALK mutations are enriched in familial neuroblastoma and represent a therapeutic target for ALK inhibitors.

biological_processes: cell surface receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway

evidence.reference_title: Coexpression of MYCN and ALK Induces Neuroblastoma-Like Tumors From Human iPS Cell-Derived Cranial Neural Crest Cells.
evidence.snippet: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) alterations, including mutations and amplification, activate oncogenic signaling pathways that, together with MYCN amplification, further enhance tumor malignancy.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of ALK as a major familial neuroblastoma predisposition gene.
evidence.snippet: Mutations resulted in constitutive phosphorylation, and targeted knockdown of ALK messenger RNA resulted in profound inhibition of growth in all cell lines harbouring mutant or amplified ALK

evidence.reference_title: ALK mutations confer differential oncogenic activation and sensitivity to ALK inhibition therapy in neuroblastoma.

ALK tyrosine kinase domain mutations occurred in 8% of samples--at three hot spots and 13 minor sites--and correlated significantly with poorer survival in high- and intermediate-risk neuroblastoma.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation-independent anaplastic lymphoma kinase overexpression in poor prognosis neuroblastoma patients.
evidence.snippet: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a receptor tyrosine kinase predominantly expressed in the developing nervous system.

evidence.reference_title: Oncogenic mutations of ALK kinase in neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: The mutated kinases were autophosphorylated and displayed increased kinase activity compared with the wild-type kinase.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation-independent anaplastic lymphoma kinase overexpression in poor prognosis neuroblastoma patients.
evidence.snippet: ALK constitutive phosphorylation/activation was observed in high-ALK expressing cells, harboring either a mutated or a wild-type receptor. No activation was found in cell lines with low expression of wild-type ALK.

evidence.reference_title: High incidence of DNA mutations and gene amplifications of the ALK gene in advanced sporadic neuroblastoma tumours.
evidence.snippet: ALK amplification or in-gene re-arrangements were found in 5% of NB tumours

evidence.reference_title: Intragenic anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) rearrangements: translocations as a novel mechanism of ALK activation in neuroblastoma tumors.
evidence.snippet: None of the translocations characterized in primary NB tumors are likely to result in a chimeric protein. However, immunohistochemical analysis reveals high levels of phosphorylated ALK in these samples despite lack of initial exons, possibly due to alternative transcription initiation sites.

evidence.reference_title: Intragenic anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) rearrangements: translocations as a novel mechanism of ALK activation in neuroblastoma tumors.
evidence.snippet: Both ALK proteins predicted to arise from such alterations and from the abnormal ALK exon 4-11 deletion observed in the CLB-BAR cell line show strong activation of downstream targets STAT3 and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) when expressed in PC12 cells.

evidence.reference_title: High anaplastic lymphoma kinase immunohistochemical staining in neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma is an independent predictor of poor outcome.
evidence.snippet: half of all NBL samples showed ALK positivity in most (>50%) of tumor cells, whereas half of the GNBL showed staining in <20% of the tumor cells

nodes.description: Mesenchymal-type neuroblastoma cells express neither mutant nor wild-type ALK, so ALK inhibition has no target in them and the escape is absence of the drug target rather than an alteration in it. The mesenchymal cells resemble immature precursor cells, which also lack ALK expression, so the absence tracks the identity state the cells occupy. This is a cell-line and xenograft result: the cells were resistant to ALK inhibitors in culture, and tumours formed from them progressed under ALK inhibitor given to the xenografted animals. No patient-level evidence is curated here.
nodes.id: ALK-Inhibitor Escape by Loss of Target Expression

evidence.reference_title: Mesenchymal-Type Neuroblastoma Cells Escape ALK Inhibitors.
evidence.snippet: MES cells did not express either mutant or wild-type ALK and were resistant to ALKi

evidence.reference_title: Mesenchymal-Type Neuroblastoma Cells Escape ALK Inhibitors.
evidence.snippet: MES cells formed tumors that progressed under ALKi therapy

nodes.description:
Neuroblastoma tumour cells occupy two transcriptionally divergent identity states, and the field names them twice over. van Groningen and colleagues name them adrenergic and mesenchymal, defined by a super-enhancer contrast between isogenic cell-line pairs. Boeva and colleagues, profiling the super-enhancer landscape of neuroblastoma cell lines, name a sympathetic noradrenergic identity whose core regulatory circuitry module includes PHOX2B, HAND2 and GATA3, an NCC-like identity driven by a circuitry module containing AP-1 transcription factors, and a mixed type. Mesenchymal and NCC-like are close but not identical concepts: the first is defined by an isogenic-pair super-enhancer contrast, the second by membership of a core regulatory circuitry.
In cell lines and xenografts the switch between the two identities arises spontaneously, runs in both directions and is accompanied by epigenetic reprogramming. The noradrenergic-to-mesenchymal shift occurs in culture; the reverse shift was documented after engraftment in mice. Enforced expression of a NOTCH3 intracellular domain drives the adrenergic-to-mesenchymal direction with genome-wide remodelling of the H3K27ac landscape, and a NOTCH feed-forward loop then maintains the induced state. SWI/SNF chromatin-remodelling ATPases are required to establish the mesenchymal gene-permissive chromatin state that facilitates this plasticity.
In patient tumours the dominant identity is noradrenergic. Gene-expression signatures derived from established cell lines fail to identify mesenchymal tumour cells in patient tumours, whereas signatures developed from early-passage orthotopic patient-derived xenografts enable their identification. A minority subpopulation of noradrenergic tumour cells co-expresses mesenchymal features, found in a subset of tumours rather than in all of them, and the mesenchymal-like programme detectable in some pre-treated high-risk patient tumours is weakly expressed, sits inside cancer cells that remain otherwise adrenergic, and appears distinct from the presumptive drug-resistance mesenchymal programmes of cell lines. Whether patient tumours also carry a discrete, purely mesenchymal tumour-cell population of the kind cultured cells show is unsettled; the evidence collected here establishes neither its presence nor its exclusion.
Microenvironmental influence is not one-directional, and the two documented cues were measured in different systems. In mouse xenografts, cells of either starting identity gave rise to tumours with a noradrenergic phenotype, which the authors read as microenvironmental pressure towards that state. In cultured cell panels, hypoxia shifted adrenergic cells towards mesenchymal gene expression.
The mesenchymal state is not the less malignant of the two: in vivo reprogramming of adrenergic cells found mesenchymal and adrenergic cells equally oncogenic.

nodes.description: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT), the recombination-based telomere maintenance mechanism that works without telomerase. Its measured frequency depends on cohort and assay: C-circle screening classified 9.2% of a 720-tumour screening cohort as ALT-positive, ALT-associated PML nuclear bodies marked 49 of 273 pretreatment neuroblastomas, and the C-circle assay marked 25 of 107 high-risk tumours from patients older than 18 months. In a registry cohort of 40 relapsed tumours, 47.5% were ALT-positive. ATRX alterations are found in only about half to 60% of ALT tumours. In primary tumours, ALT and the routes to telomerase activation occur almost mutually exclusively, and ATRX mutation and MYCN amplification co-occurred in only 1 of 819 tumours. ALT-positive neuroblastomas proliferate slowly, with a protracted clinical course, yet children with these tumours have a dismal outcome. About a third of ALT-positive tumours present with localized disease classified as low or intermediate risk, and in one cohort survival did not differ between ALT-positive tumours classified high risk and those classified low or intermediate risk.

Dinutuximab is the licensed agent in the United States and dinutuximab beta in Europe. The contribution of the two cytokines is not settled in the way the antibody's is: in the European HR-NBL1/SIOPEN randomization, adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta gave no event-free survival benefit and added toxicity, and the trialists recommended the regimen without it as the standard of care, while the United States label still lists interleukin-2. No trial has ever isolated GM-CSF's own contribution. The benefit is therefore recorded here as a regimen-level effect of anti-GD2-based immunotherapy rather than as an effect of any one component. nodes.description: N-Myc protein is short-lived: degradation requires sequential phosphorylation by cyclin B/Cdk1 and GSK3, after which the SCF(Fbxw7) ubiquitin ligase ubiquitinates it for proteasomal destruction. Aurora A binds both N-Myc and that ligase and counteracts the degradation, which uncouples N-Myc abundance from the growth-factor signalling that would otherwise set it. The stabilising action does not need Aurora A's kinase activity: it is a protein-protein interaction, and inhibitors that merely block the catalytic site lower N-Myc only modestly, whereas compounds that distort the kinase's native conformation drive N-Myc degradation. An shRNA screen found AURKA required for the growth of MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cells and largely dispensable without amplification, which is what makes the interaction a dependency rather than an incidental one. What does not follow is the therapeutic corollary: in the clinic, alisertib has done worse in MYCN-amplified disease than in non-amplified disease, the opposite of what this mechanism predicts. That tension is recorded as a human-model mismatch discussion rather than smoothed over here.

nodes.description: Autoimmunity held to be directed at the cerebellum and brainstem and to involve B and T lymphocytes. Children with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome (OMS), most with normal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cell counts, have expanded B-cell and gamma-delta T-cell subsets and a higher percentage of activated T cells in the CSF. In a cross-sectional cohort the subset expansion was found even years after onset and conventional treatment, the abnormalities correlated with neurological severity and disease duration, they did not differ significantly between children with and without a tumor, and, in children with neuroblastoma, tumor resection or chemotherapy did not alter them. In a larger cohort of 389 children from the same investigators, commercial serum paraneoplastic antibody panels were negative apart from subclinical titers in four children, whereas in untreated children CSF oligoclonal bands (58%) and a raised CSF B-cell percentage (93%) were common. No specific antibody is associated with neuroblastoma-associated OMS, and a study of OMAS-associated tumors identified no unifying single antigen behind their lymphoid infiltrate. Most of the CSF findings come from cohorts of children with and without a detected tumor.

nodes.description: Neuroblastoma cells import polyamines from the surrounding microenvironment, which is the reason blocking synthesis does not deplete them. Treating neuroblastoma cells with the ODC1 inhibitor eflornithine (DFMO) is only partially effective against cell growth, because compensatory mechanisms raise polyamine uptake; in culture, polyamines taken from the medium rescue the deficit the drug creates. SLC3A2 was identified as the key transporter carrying that uptake in neuroblastoma, knocking it down lowered uptake of radiolabelled spermidine, and DFMO treatment itself raised SLC3A2 protein, so the drug induces the route around its own target. Blocking uptake with AMXT 1501 alongside DFMO prevented or delayed tumour development in neuroblastoma-prone mice and extended survival in rodent models of established tumours, and in a second laboratory the same combination deepened the inhibition of protein synthesis even in cell lines resistant to high-dose DFMO alone. Marked PROVISIONAL because every result here is from cell lines or rodent models: nothing establishes that uptake limits the approved drug's effect in patients. The synthesis arm is the Polyamine Biosynthesis Dependence node, and what the approval does and does not settle is in the Eflornithine treatment record.

nodes.description: First-generation ATP-competitive ALK/MET inhibitor, and the first ALK inhibitor tested in neuroblastoma. nodes.description: In MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma the supernumerary MYCN copies are commonly carried on extrachromosomal circular DNA (ecDNA), which can be highly rearranged. The extrachromosomal form is the common state and not the only one: the same paper reports a MYCN amplicon carried as a linear intrachromosomal array, a homogeneously staining region. Amplicon composition is not random. Across a copy-number meta-dataset of 240 MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas, a 290 kb region downstream of MYCN was co-amplified in more than 90% of tumours, and the distal MYCN-specific enhancer e4, driven by the noradrenergic core regulatory circuit (CRC), lay inside the consensus amplicon in 90% of cases. Two amplicon classes follow. The first always co-amplifies a proximal CRC-driven enhancer; the second is structurally complex, lacks the key local enhancers and instead carries distal chromosomal fragments harbouring CRC-driven enhancers, which the authors read as ectopic enhancer hijacking replacing the missing local elements. That classification was made on primary-tumour copy-number profiles, which cannot separate extrachromosomal from intrachromosomal amplicons, so it applies to both forms. The two classes were prognostically indistinguishable in the same series, so amplicon class sets the regulatory route to MYCN overexpression rather than clinical behaviour. Separately, rearrangements derived from extrachromosomal circles can give rise to cancer-causing lesions and are associated with adverse clinical outcome; that association belongs to the circle-derived rearrangements and not to amplicon class.

nodes.description: Mesenchymal-state cells survive cytotoxic chemotherapy that kills adrenergic cells, and mesenchymal features have been reported to become enriched after chemotherapy and at relapse while adrenergic traits predominate in untreated tumours. nodes.description: The subset of neuroblastomas enriched for immune-related transcripts is predominantly characterised by mesenchymal lineage gene-expression signatures, while tumours expressing adrenergic lineage signatures are less immunogenic by the same measures. nodes.description: Spread of neuroblastoma cells from the primary tumor to distant sites, where they establish metastases. In 648 children with stage IV or IVS disease on two Children's Cancer Group protocols, metastases at diagnosis were in bone marrow (70.5%), bone (55.7%), lymph nodes (30.9%), liver (29.6%), and intracranial and orbital sites (18.2%), and rarely in lung or the central nervous system. nodes.description: Loss of NGF-dependent TrkA signalling in the neuroblasts of a TRKA-expressing tumour, the cellular state on which the neurotrophin-deprivation account of spontaneous regression rests. Many more sympathetic neuronal precursors are produced during normal development than are needed, and those that fail to reach a target undergo developmentally programmed cell death, a process set primarily by the TrkA neurotrophin receptor and the limiting availability of its ligand NGF at the target site. Tumours from infants, especially with low-stage or 4S disease, generally express high levels of TrkA, and in patient tumours high TRK expression goes with favourable stage, age under one year and normal MYCN copy number. Cells cultured from TRK-expressing tumours survive and differentiate when NGF is supplied and die when it is withheld. Why TrkA-expressing favourable tumours survive at all despite a lack of available NGF is unresolved: a developmentally programmed switch from the ligand-independent TrkAIII isoform to TrkAI has been proposed as the step that makes such a tumour NGF-dependent. The node commits to no mode of death; that step is carried by the downstream edge, whose intermediate mechanisms state what has been measured and where.

nodes.description: Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome (OMAS), also called opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome (OMS), classically combines a characteristic eye-movement disorder (opsoclonus) and myoclonus with ataxia, irritability and sleep disturbance. There is good evidence that it is immune-mediated, and with neuroblastoma it may be paraneoplastic. It develops in a small minority of children with neuroblastoma: 9 of 405 children in a Hospital for Sick Children series and 21 of 675 children in a Children's Cancer Group questionnaire study of patients whose sera were banked at diagnosis, while 15 of 1,187 children with previously untreated neuroblastic tumors in an Italian registry had it at presentation. More recent figures are 2.7% of neuroblastoma presentations in a meta-analysis of mainly abdominal neuroblastoma series published from 2005 to 2023, 4.7% of 776 children with peripheral neuroblastic tumors across 14 Polish centers, and 12 of 189 children with neuroblastoma (6.3%) at one tertiary care center in India. It can be the presenting sign of an occult, localized tumor. In the cited series the associated tumors were mostly non-metastatic, mostly of favorable histology and mostly without MYCN amplification, and ganglioneuroblastoma was common among them. Survival in these series was excellent, but many children were left with developmental or neurological sequelae. Read the other way, a neuroblastic tumor, most often neuroblastoma, is found in roughly 40-50% of children with OMAS in recent series; that proportion has a different denominator and does not set the frequency band.

nodes.description: Growth of the primary tumor at its site of origin along the sympathetic nervous system, and the pressure it exerts on, or its growth into, neighboring structures. About three-quarters of primary tumors arise in the abdomen or pelvis, half of these in the adrenal medulla, about a fifth in the posterior mediastinum and about a twentieth in the neck, and the local signs follow from the site. An abdominal primary can present as a palpable abdominal mass, abdominal distension or abdominal pain. A paravertebral tumor can grow through the neural foramina into the spinal canal and compress the spinal cord or nerve roots. Horner syndrome is seen mostly with localized disease, often with cervical or thoracic tumors, and is attributed to mass effect of the tumor on the sympathetic innervation of the eye. Compression of the renal artery or renal parenchyma is the usual explanation offered for hypertension at diagnosis, but a registry survey of hypertensive children could not demonstrate a correlation between hypertension and compression of the renal vascular pedicle. Cells leaving the primary tumor give rise to metastases at distant sites.

nodes.description: Ligand-independent flux through the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade, driven by activating lesions in NRAS, KRAS, HRAS, BRAF, PTPN11 or FGFR1, or by inactivation of the RAS GTPase-activating protein NF1. These lesions are enriched in relapse tumours rather than specific to them. Whole-genome sequencing of 23 matched diagnostic and relapse neuroblastomas found mutations predicted to activate the pathway in 18 of the 23 relapse tumours (78%), a figure that counts ALK, which this entry models on its own ALK Signaling Activation node and which accounted for 10 of the 18; the other 8 were NF1 inactivation in two tumours and NRAS, KRAS, HRAS, BRAF, PTPN11 and FGFR1 alterations in one each, one lesion per tumour because no tumour carried more than one. Seven of the 18 events were not detected in the matched diagnostic tumour by whole-genome sequencing, and deeper testing of those primaries recovered two, so 13 of the 18 were detectable at diagnosis. At diagnosis the same mutations are uncommon and mostly subclonal: an ultra-deep panel covering NRAS, KRAS, HRAS, BRAF and PTPN11 found them in 7.9% of 242 pretherapy high-risk tumours, 15 of the 19 below that study's 20% variant-allele-frequency cut-off for clonality. A pan-paediatric paired series adds NF1 as a lesion selected at relapse; that cohort's finding that lesions outside these two classes are also selected at relapse is recorded on the Relapsed or Refractory Disease progression phase rather than here.

nodes.description: Reduced abundance of the ATRX/DAXX chromatin remodelling complex, a recurrent molecular feature of alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) in neuroblastoma. ATRX encodes an ATP-dependent helicase of the SWI/SNF family of chromatin remodellers and, with DAXX, deposits the histone variant H3.3 at telomeric regions. ALT-positive neuroblastomas show reduced ATRX/DAXX complex abundance, due either to ATRX mutation (55% of them in one cohort) or to low protein expression, while mutations in the complex members DAXX and H3F3A were extremely rare. In a pooled analysis of published ATRX-altered neuroblastomas, 68% of ATRX aberrations were multi-exon deletions, and 75% of these were predicted to be in-frame. nodes.description: Neuroblastoma cells carry enough replication stress that they depend on the S and G2 checkpoint to survive it. CDK1 is held in check by CHK1 and WEE1, which buy time for repair before mitosis and let the cell tolerate stressed replication; removing either kinase collapses replication forks or forces an unprepared mitosis. A loss-of-function screen across the protein kinome found CHK1 the most potent of thirty cytotoxic hits in neuroblastoma, and the checkpoint is demonstrably running in patient material rather than only in culture: CHK1 was constitutively phosphorylated at Ser345 and Ser296 in six of eight high-risk primary tumours and in only one of eight low-risk ones. The dependence tracks N-Myc, since inhibitor sensitivity followed total MYC(N) protein and inducing MYCN in untransformed cells was by itself enough to phosphorylate CHK1. The node is marked PROVISIONAL because the disease-specific dependency rests largely on one screen and its follow-up assays, and because the clinical test of it has so far produced few responses in heavily pre-treated children.

nodes.description: Involution of a neuroblastoma, or its maturation toward ganglioneuroblastoma or ganglioneuroma, without cytotoxic treatment. It is seen mainly in infants whose tumours lack MYCN amplification, with localized disease or the 4S/MS pattern of metastasis: in the prospective NB95-S and NB97 trials, 44 of the 93 infants observed with gross residual localized tumour regressed spontaneously, with first signs 1 to 18 months after diagnosis and, in 15 of the 44, after the first year of life. Regression in this entry covers maturation as well as shrinkage, because among mass-screened localized adrenal tumours left in place, the six resected after one to four years of observation had all matured toward ganglioneuroblastoma, which the authors call a common phenomenon; 16 of 45 resected in infancy showed the same change. It is not universal in the 4S pattern: of 268 evaluable Italian infants with stage 4S disease, 29 progressed at 4S sites and 28 progressed to stage 4. Mass screening gives a figure for how much disease screening finds that never needed finding rather than a count of regressions: screening at about one year of age produced an estimated 7 overdiagnosed cases per 100,000 children, while stage 4 incidence and neuroblastoma mortality stayed similar to the unscreened control states. That estimate mixes tumours that would have regressed with tumours that would have stayed silent, and it cannot see tumours that regressed before the screening age or after clinical diagnosis, so it neither measures nor cleanly bounds regression. This node is the phenomenon rather than a mechanism; which mechanism produces it is unsettled, and the competing candidates are recorded as the entry's mechanistic hypothesis groups, two of which carry an edge into this node.

nodes.description: The ability of tumour cells to keep dividing indefinitely, which a telomere maintenance mechanism (telomerase activation or ALT) provides. Its binding, increased cell population proliferation, follows the module node it conforms to and means expansion continuing past the limit that telomere shortening sets on normal cells, not a faster division rate: ALT-positive neuroblastomas proliferate more slowly than telomerase-activated ones. Aggressive neuroblastomas show a prolonged evolution during which they acquire telomere maintenance mechanisms, whereas tumours with a favourable prognosis expand clonally after a short evolution. In pretreatment neuroblastomas, patients whose tumours lacked a telomere maintenance mechanism had an excellent prognosis and those whose tumours had one did substantially worse. nodes.description: The mature let-7 microRNA family is depleted in neuroblastoma by three routes that substitute for one another rather than acting in series: LIN28B blockade of let-7 maturation; sponging of let-7 by the MYCN transcript, which in MYCN-amplified disease reaches levels high enough to titrate the family; and genetic loss of let-7 loci, which is common in neuroblastoma, inversely associated with MYCN amplification and independently associated with poor outcomes. let-7 represses MYCN post-transcriptionally, so depleting it de-represses MYCN and lifts the let-7 restraint on neuroblast differentiation. The routes converge on this node, which is why an entry whose flagship subtype is MYCN-amplified disease cannot model the LIN28B route alone.

animal_models.description: The model runs the LIN28B-to-let-7 arm forwards: driving LIN28B in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage produces tumours whose let-7 is low and whose MYCN protein is high.

nodes.description: Loss of p53-axis control, through an inactivating TP53 mutation, MDM2 amplification (in the SIOPEN cohort cited here as CDK4/MDM2 co-amplification, the two genes lying at 12q14.1 and 12q15; in the relapse series cited here as MDM2 amplification alone at 12q15), or homozygous CDKN2A deletion removing p14ARF. In 84 tumours from 41 patients with relapsed neuroblastoma, a p53-pathway abnormality was detected in 20 of 41 (49%) cases. That is a share of patients who relapsed rather than of relapse tumours, and it is a floor, because MDM2 amplification was assessed in only 23 of the roughly 35 patients whose relapse tumour was p53-wild-type and TP53 sequencing covered exons 4-9. The parts of the pathway differ in timing: TP53 mutations were first detected after chemotherapy in all but one of the six mutated cases, whereas MDM2 amplification and p14ARF inactivation were present at both diagnosis and relapse in most cases, so this is not a uniformly therapy-era lesion. The p14ARF readout in that series was specific to CDKN2A exon 1-beta, the p53-arm product, whereas p16INK4a from the same locus acts in the RB arm. The pathway is not confined to MYCN-amplified disease: in a SIOPEN series of 98 non-MYCN-amplified, localized unresectable or stage 3 tumours of unfavourable histology, classed as intermediate risk under the European criteria used there and, in the paper's own words, as high risk in most of North America, 10 tumours carried a p53-pathway abnormality and those patients had inferior event-free and overall survival. That study's definition of the abnormality also admits a pathogenic ATM mutation, which this node does not bind.

nodes.description: The common intronic LIN28B risk allele at 6q16, reported with a combined odds ratio of 1.38 (95% CI 1.23-1.54) across a North American discovery cohort, an Italian replication cohort and an African American cohort. Carried here as a structured variant so the rsID and effect size are queryable rather than held in prose. No clinical_significance is set: the enum's values describe Mendelian variant classification, and a common risk allele of this effect size is none of them.

evidence.reference_title: Common variation at 6q16 within HACE1 and LIN28B influences susceptibility to neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report a genome-wide association study of 2,817 neuroblastoma cases and 7,473 controls. We identified two new associations at 6q16 ... the second within LIN28B (rs17065417; combined P=1.2×10(-8); odds ratio 1.38, 95% CI 1.23-1.54).
